info.title: Midwater API
info.summary: Send each finished AI-agent conversation to Midwater and read back its outcome, check results and agent health.
info.description:
Midwater checks every conversation your AI agents have, voice calls and chats. Send each finished
conversation with its transcript; Midwater scores it in the background and you read the outcome,
the result of every check, and each agent's health.

**Authentication.** Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A key belongs to one environment
of one project: test keys start `mw_test_`, live keys `mw_live_`. Keys made before October 2026 start `vk_` and still work.

**Base URL.** `https://api.midwater.ai` (the `servers` entry). Your key decides the project and environment (test or live), so there's one host for both.

**Versioning.** The version is in the path (`/v1`). Adding fields, endpoints, event types or enum values
doesn't change the version, so accept values you don't recognise. A breaking change gets `/v2`, with at
least 6 months of overlap.
This document's own `info.version` is plain semver: a patch for spec-only fixes, a minor for added fields,
endpoints or values, and a major that matches the path.

**Errors.** Every error is JSON: `{ "error": { "type", "message", "fields"?, "request_id" } }`, with a fixed
list of types and status codes. Treat an unknown type by its status class. Planned: every `/v1` path answers
JSON errors, including unknown paths (`404 not_found`) and unsupported methods (`405 method_not_allowed`, with
an `Allow` header); today those two answer without a JSON body. Routes that aren't available yet answer
`501 not_implemented` with a link to the public docs.

**Planned renames.** Three values get new names (planned; both old and new are listed in the enums, and the
SDKs accept both): `decided_by` `llm_judge` → `second_review`; `outcome` `escalated` → `handed_to_person`;
`outcome` `not_real_inquiry` → `not_customer_call`. The field name `verdict` stays.

**Pagination.** None in v1. When list endpoints arrive they are cursor-based: `limit` and `cursor` in,
`{ "data", "next_cursor" }` out.

**Planned behaviour.** Anything marked `x-status: planned` is agreed but not yet built. Don't rely on it yet.
Each operation's `x-midwater-verified` is the date it was last checked against a running Midwater stack.

post.description:
Stores a finished call or chat and queues it for scoring. Answers `202` with `status: "queued"`;
read the result with `GET /v1/conversations/{id}` or wait for the `conversation.evaluated` webhook.

Sending an `external_id` that already exists in this environment answers `200` with the existing
conversation and `duplicate: true`; nothing new is created.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe: a repeated key in the same environment
answers with the first response and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

A conversation without `agent.id` goes to the project's Default agent (ID `default`). A new
`agent.id` creates the agent the first time it's seen.

200.description: A conversation with this `external_id` already exists in this environment; it is returned instead of a duplicate.

get.summary: Get a conversation and its results
get.description:
Returns the conversation, its scoring `status`, its `outcome` and the result of every check.
`id` is Midwater's ID or your `external_id`. Results appear once `status` is `done`.

post.summary: Confirm or correct a check result
post.description:
Records your team's answer for one check on one conversation (stored as a label with source `api`).
`id` is Midwater's ID or your `external_id`. Today each call adds a label; idempotency keys on this
endpoint are planned.

apiKey.description: An API key: `mw_test_…` for the test environment, `mw_live_…` for live.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Any string unique to this request (255 characters or fewer), for example your `external_id`. Kept for 24 hours per
environment. Repeating the key with the same request (the same endpoint and the same JSON body, in any key order)
answers with the first response and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; nothing is created twice. Reusing it with a different
request answers `409 idempotency_conflict`. Only successful responses are kept: a request that failed validation can
be corrected and sent again with the same key. Honoured on every `POST`.

MidwaterSignature.name: Midwater-Signature
MidwaterSignature.description: `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`: HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` keyed with the environment's signing secret (`whsec_…`). Verify with a 5-minute tolerance and a constant-time compare, and accept the delivery if any `v1=` value matches.

MidwaterEvent.name: Midwater-Event
MidwaterEvent.description: The event type, the same as the body's `type`.

MidwaterDelivery.name: Midwater-Delivery
MidwaterDelivery.description: The delivery ID; the same on every retry of one delivery. Deduplicate on it.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when this response is a replay of an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

RequestId.description: The request's ID, also in error bodies as `error.request_id`. Quote it when contacting support.

Allow.description: The methods the path supports, e.g. `POST`.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed in the current window. The numbers are published when the limits are set.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, unknown or revoked API key.

error.message: Missing or invalid API key. Use Authorization: Bearer mw_test_… or mw_live_…

PermissionDenied.description: The key is valid but not allowed to do this.

ValidationError.description: The body is JSON but doesn't match the schema. `fields` maps each dotted path to its messages.

transcript: transcript needs at least one turn

NotFound.description: Not found in the key's environment.

IdempotencyConflict.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used in this environment, within 24 hours, for a different request (another endpoint or a different body). Use a new key for a new request.

error.message: This Idempotency-Key was already used for a different request. Use a new key for a new request.

PayloadTooLarge.description: The body is larger than the limit. The limit is published when it's set.

error.message: The request body is too large

RateLimited.description: Too many requests. Wait `Retry-After` seconds. The limits are published when they're set.

ServerError.description: Something went wrong on Midwater's side. Safe to retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

error.message: Something went wrong on our side

ServiceUnavailable.description: Midwater is briefly unavailable. Retry with backoff, honouring `Retry-After` when present.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but doesn't support this method. `Allow` lists the methods it does support.

error.message: GET isn't supported here; use POST

type.description:
Stable machine-readable type. Each has a set status: `invalid_json` 400, `authentication_error` 401,
`permission_denied` 403, `not_found` 404, `method_not_allowed` 405, `idempotency_conflict` 409, `payload_too_large` 413,
`validation_error` 422, `rate_limited` 429, `server_error` 500, `service_unavailable` 503.
Types not yet returned are planned. Treat a type you don't know by its status class.

fields.description: Validation errors by dotted path, e.g. `transcript.0.speaker`. `_root` for the body as a whole.

request_id.description: The request's ID, the same as the `Midwater-Request-Id` header.

SafeId.description: A letter or digit, then up to 127 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:` or `-`. No `/`, so IDs never need URL-encoding.

Speaker.description: `agent` is your AI agent, `user` the caller or chat user, `human_agent` a person who took over.

start_ms.description: Offset from the start of the conversation.

Event.description: Something your agent did: a tool call, a transfer, a handoff. Extra properties are kept. The built-in booking checks turn on the first time a `tool_call` whose `name` contains `book` or `schedul` arrives. A `transfer` or `handoff` event marks the conversation as handed to a person.

AgentRef.description: The AI agent that handled the conversation. Omit it to use the project's Default agent.

name.description: Shown in Midwater; used when the agent is first created.

version.description: Your agent's release, e.g. `3.2.0`. Releases are marked on the agent's trend.

GroupRef.description: Files the agent into this group (created if needed) the first time the agent is seen without one. Ignored once someone places the agent in the app.

external_id.description: Your ID for this call or chat. Unique per environment.

ended_at.description: Defaults to the time Midwater received it.

ended_by.description: Who ended the conversation. `timeout` is valid for chat only.

metadata.description: Anything else you want kept with the conversation.

ConversationStatus.description: Scoring status. `failed` means scoring didn't finish after Midwater's automatic retries (five attempts in all); it can be re-run from the app.

duplicate.description: Present and `true` when the `external_id` already existed.

Outcome.description:
How the conversation ended for the caller. `resolved`: Resolved. `unresolved`: Unresolved.
`escalated`: Handed to a person. `not_real_inquiry`: Not a customer call (sales, spam, wrong number),
kept out of resolution rates. `null` while scoring, or when no outcome check applied.
Planned renames: `escalated` becomes `handed_to_person` and `not_real_inquiry` becomes `not_customer_call`;
accept both until the change is announced in the changelog.

CheckResultValue.description:
`pass`: no problem found. `fail`: Midwater found this problem. `uncertain`: unclear; a person should look.
`not_applicable`: didn't apply to this conversation. `met` / `not_met`: for gating questions
(for example, whether this was a real customer inquiry).

DecidedBy.description: `rule`: decided from the events you sent. `model`: Midwater's model read the whole conversation. `llm_judge`: a second review for unclear conversations (planned rename: `second_review`; accept both). `human`: someone on your team.

check_key.description: Stable key of the check; use it with the feedback endpoint.

check_status.description: `shadow` checks are scored but never alert.

score.description: Likelihood that the problem occurred, 0 to 1.

choice.description: The chosen option for multiple-choice checks.

reason.description: One or two sentences on why.

evidence_turns.description: The transcript turns the result points to.

scorer_version.description: Midwater's opaque version of how the result was scored, e.g. `2026-10-06.3`. `null` when nothing scored the result (a check that didn't apply, or wasn't evaluated).

dashboard_url.description: The conversation in the Midwater app.

verdict.description: Your team's answer: `pass` (no problem) or `fail` (the problem happened).

HealthStatus.description: `not_enough_calls`: fewer than 5 calls with an outcome in the last 7 days, so nothing is measured yet, unless a high-severity compliance failure puts the agent in `watch` (1) or `at_risk` (2 or more).

with_outcome.description: Conversations with an outcome (customer calls that were scored).

resolution_rate.description: Share of conversations with an outcome that were resolved.

handed_to_person_rate.description: Share handed to a person (a transfer, or a person requested and provided).

requests_for_person_not_honored.description: Conversations where the caller asked for a person and didn't get one.

compliance_failures.description: Compliance checks that failed in the window.

environment.description: The key's environment; health is measured per environment.

reason.description: Why, in one sentence, e.g. "Needs 4 more calls with an outcome this week".
Watch and at risk name the agent that set the status.

environment.description: Webhooks fire for live conversations, and for test ones only when the destination or route opts in.

agent.description: The agent whose status set the group's.

Coverage.description: How much of the transcript Midwater read. A very long call (roughly over 90 minutes of clean talk, or 70 of messy talk) can be read in part: one stretch from the middle is skipped and the opening and ending are kept. Checks answered from the partial transcript may be incomplete. `complete: true` means the whole transcript was read.

skipped_turns.description: How many turns in the middle weren't read (0 when complete).

skipped_from.description: Milliseconds from the start of the call: the first skipped turn's `start_ms`. `null` when complete or when the turns have no times.

skipped_to.description: Milliseconds from the start of the call: the last skipped turn's `end_ms` (or its `start_ms`). `null` when complete or when the turns have no times.
